outcomeNote: Two more bare mishnaic clauses in the chapter's series of inversions, with no dispute, no named party and no argument.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַתֶּמֶד, עַד שֶׁלֹּא הֶחְמִיץ – אֵינוֹ נִיקָּח בְּכֶסֶף מַעֲשֵׂר, וּפוֹסֵל אֶת הַמִּקְוֶה. מִשֶּׁהֶחְמִיץ – נִיקָּח בְּכֶסֶף מַעֲשֵׂר, וְאֵינוֹ פּוֹסֵל אֶת הַמִּקְוֶה.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «Temed,» a beverage produced from grape residue soaked in water, «until it fermented, may not be purchased with» second-«tithe money» to be drunk in Jerusalem, because it is not wine. «And» if three log of it fall into a ritual bath, its halakhic status is that of drawn water and «it invalidates the ritual bath. Once it fermented, it» is wine, and therefore it «may be purchased with» second-«tithe money and it does not invalidate the ritual bath.»

segments.he: הָאַחִין הַשּׁוּתָּפִין, כְּשֶׁחַיָּיבִין בַּקָּלְבּוֹן – פְּטוּרִין מִמַּעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה; כְּשֶׁחַיָּיבִין בְּמַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה – פְּטוּרִין מִן הַקָּלְבּוֹן.
segments.en: With regard to «brothers who are partners» in the inheritance of their father, «when they are obligated to» add «the premium [kalbon]» to their annual half-shekel payment to the Temple, «they are exempt from animal tithe; when they are obligated to» separate «animal tithe, they are exempt from» adding «the premium.» Partners who pay the half-shekel are required to add the premium and are exempt from animal tithe. If they are not true partners, but their inheritance remains the property of the father, the sons are exempt from paying the premium, and they are obligated to separate animal tithe.

moves.summary: states the inversion for temed before and after fermentation, as tithe money and as drawn water
states the inversion for brothers who are partners between the half-shekel premium and animal tithe
